claims.claim: Genes that show increased expression in Emx2 Cre/Cre utricles are likely to be transcriptionally repressed by EMX2.
claims.source: Genes that show increased expression in Emx2 Cre/Cre utricles are likely to be transcriptionally repressed by EMX2, through either direct or indirect mechanisms, and may also contribute to hair cell patterning about the LPR (Supplementary file 2).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the RNAseq data.

claims.claim: Stk32a/Yank1 is expressed in the medial region of the utricle and outer region of the saccule in a pattern complementary to that of Emx2.
claims.source: One such candidate was Stk32a/Yank1 which is expressed in the medial region of the utricle and outer region of the saccule in a pattern complementary to that of Emx2 when visualized by fluorescent in situ hybridization (fISH) (Figure 1I and J).
claims.evidence: This is supported by fluorescent in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1I and J.

claims.claim: STK32A is a serine threonine kinase with sequence similarity to AGC kinases and is a member of a small kinase protein family that includes STK32B/YANK2 and STK32C/YANK3.
claims.source: STK32A is a serine threonine kinase with sequence similarity to AGC kinases and is a member of a small kinase protein family that includes STK32B/YANK2 and STK32C/YANK3.
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about the STK32 kinase family.

claims.claim: The STK32 kinases have been categorized as dark kinases because their substrates and biological functions are not known.
claims.source: The STK32 kinases have been categorized as dark kinases because their substrates and biological functions are not known (Berginski et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior literature.

claims.claim: Stk32a mRNA was detected in clusters that overlapped with mRNA transcribed from the hair cell gene Gfi1.
claims.source: Within the developing utricle, Stk32a mRNA was detected in clusters that overlapped with mRNA transcribed from the hair cell gene Gfi1 (Figure 1K).
claims.evidence: This is supported by fluorescent in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1K.

claims.claim: A similar pattern of Stk32a expression was seen in the semi-circular canal cristae.
claims.source: A similar pattern of expression was seen in the semi-circular canal cristae (Figure 1L and M).
claims.evidence: This is supported by fluorescent in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1L and M.

claims.claim: Hair cells in the semi-circular canal cristae lack EMX2 and have stereociliary bundles oriented with the kinocilium positioned opposite of PK2 similar to utricular hair cells located medial to the LPR.
claims.source: The hair cells in each of these regions lack EMX2 and have stereociliary bundles oriented with the kinocilium positioned opposite of PK2 similar to utricular hair cells located medial to the LPR (Deans et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior literature.

claims.claim: The increase in Stk32a mRNA detected by RNAseq is due to an expansion of the Stk32a expression domain.
claims.source: The increase in Stk32a mRNA detected by RNAseq is due to an expansion of the Stk32a expression domain and in the absence of Emx2, Stk32a mRNA can be detected throughout the entire sensory epithelia (Figure 2A and B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by fluorescent in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claims.claim: In the absence of Emx2, Stk32a mRNA can be detected throughout the entire sensory epithelia.
claims.source: The increase in Stk32a mRNA detected by RNAseq is due to an expansion of the Stk32a expression domain and in the absence of Emx2, Stk32a mRNA can be detected throughout the entire sensory epithelia (Figure 2A and B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by fluorescent in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claims.claim: When Emx2 is ectopically expressed in hair cells throughout the sensory epithelia using Gfi1-Cre crossed with LSL-Emx2 overexpression mice, Stk32a expression is reduced wherever Emx2 is induced.
claims.source: Conversely, when Emx2 is ectopically expressed in hair cells throughout the sensory epithelia using hair cell-restricted Gfi1-Cre crossed with Lox-Stop-Lox (LSL) Emx2 overexpression mice (Rosa26 LSL-Emx2), Stk32a expression is reduced wherever Emx2 is induced (Jiang et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 2F, G, I, J and citation to prior work.

claims.claim: Stk32a is a gene negatively regulated in the lateral region of the utricle resulting in non-overlapping and complementary patterns of Emx2 and Stk32a.
claims.source: Together these gene expression studies identify Stk32a as a gene negatively regulated in the lateral region of the utricle resulting in non-overlapping and complementary patterns of Emx2 and Stk32a.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the gene expression data presented.

claims.claim: Hair cells located in the lateral utricle transduced at P0 with AAVs expressing Stk32a-P2A-EGFP showed prominent changes in bundle orientation with many lateral hair cells having orientations that resembled hair cells from the medial utricle.
claims.source: In contrast to controls, hair cells located in the lateral utricle transduced at P0 with AAVs expressing Stk32a-P2A-EGFP showed prominent changes in bundle orientation with many lateral hair cells having orientations that resembled hair cells from the medial utricle (Figure 3B,B',F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by AAV overexpression data shown in Figure 3.

claims.claim: When lateral hair cells were transduced at P5 with Stk32a-P2A-EGFP, fewer reversed cells were present suggesting that the impact of ectopic STK32A might be age dependent.
claims.source: When lateral hair cells were transduced at P5 with Stk32a-P2A-EGFP (Figure 3E,E',F), fewer reversed cells were present suggesting that the impact of ectopic STK32A might be age dependent.
claims.evidence: This is supported by AAV overexpression data shown in Figure 3E, E', F.

claims.claim: STK32A acts during stereociliary bundle morphogenesis and is less capable of reorienting the bundle once the structure has matured.
claims.source: Most likely this is because STK32A acts during stereociliary bundle morphogenesis and is less capable of reorienting the bundle once the structure has matured.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the age-dependent effects of STK32A overexpression.

claims.claim: The effect of STK32A on bundle orientation is dependent upon the kinase activity of STK32A.
claims.source: This effect is also likely dependent upon the kinase activity of STK32A because it is disrupted by substituting the Lysine residue that facilitates ATP-binding prior to substrate phosphorylation with Arginine (K52R) (Sorrell et al., 2020; UniProt Consortium, 2021).
claims.evidence: This is supported by data showing that the K52R mutant cannot reorient hair cells, and by citations to prior literature about kinase function.

claims.claim: AAV expressing Stk32 K52R-P2A-EGFP was incapable of reorienting hair cells in the lateral region of the utricle when introduced to utricle explants at P0.
claims.source: Consistent with this, AAV expressing Stk32 K52R-P2A-EGFP was incapable of reorienting hair cells in the lateral region of the utricle when introduced to utricle explants at P0 (Figure 3C,C',F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by AAV overexpression data shown in Figure 3C, C', F.

claims.claim: STK32A::EGFP was detected in the apical compartment of transduced hair cells and stereociliary bundle.
claims.source: Using this approach, STK32A::EGFP was detected in the apical compartment of transduced hair cells and stereociliary bundle (Figure 3G, H).
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 3G, H.

claims.claim: STK32A::EGFP can be detected in the apical compartment between 12 hr and 24 hr post-transduction and continues to be enriched in this area despite increased STK32A::EGFP labeling throughout the hair cell over the subsequent 48 hr.
claims.source: STK32A::EGFP can be detected in this apical compartment between 12 hr and 24 hr post-transduction and continues to be enriched in this area despite increased STK32A::EGFP labeling throughout the hair cell over the subsequent 48 hr.
claims.evidence: This is based on observations of STK32A::EGFP distribution over time.

claims.claim: EGFP alone remained cytosolic and strictly labeled the cell soma.
claims.source: This is in contrast to EGFP alone which remained cytosolic and strictly labeled the cell soma (Figure 3A–E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 3A-E.

claims.claim: Motif-based evaluation of the STK32A primary amino acid sequence identified the potential for myristoylation of the Glycine located at amino acid position 2.
claims.source: Motif-based evaluation of the STK32A primary amino acid sequence also identified the potential for myristoylation of the Glycine located at amino acid position 2.
claims.evidence: This is based on computational sequence analysis.

claims.claim: STK32AΔ2G::EGFP was not enriched in the stereociliary bundle.
claims.source: When evaluated in transduced hair cells STK32AΔ2G::EGFP was not enriched in the stereociliary bundle (Figure 3F,I,I',J,J').
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 3F, I, I', J, J'.

claims.claim: STK32AΔ2G::EGFP was not capable of reversing the orientation of hair cells in the lateral utricle indicating that STK32A needs to be located at the apical cell surface to have this affect.
claims.source: Moreover, STK32AΔ2G::EGFP was not capable of reversing the orientation of hair cells in the lateral utricle indicating that STK32A needs to be located at the apical cell surface to have this affect (Figure 3D, D' and F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by AAV overexpression data shown in Figure 3D, D', F.

claims.claim: The distribution of STK32A::EGFP fusion proteins and the capability of STK32A::EGFP to generate hair cells with medial bundle orientations in the lateral utricle suggests that endogenous STK32A functions in the apical compartment of developing hair cells.
claims.source: Together, the distribution of these STK32A::EGFP fusion proteins and the capability of STK32A::EGFP to generate hair cells with medial bundle orientations in the lateral utricle suggests that endogenous STK32A functions in the apical compartment of developing hair cells.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the localization and functional data for STK32A::EGFP.

claims.claim: Stk32a -/- mice were viable, survived to adulthood and showed no overt physical or behavioral differences from littermate controls.
claims.source: When the deletion was homozygosed, Stk32a -/- mice were viable, survived to adulthood and showed no overt physical or behavioral differences from littermate controls.
claims.evidence: This is based on observations of Stk32a -/- mice.

claims.claim: No differences were detected in the planar polarized organization of utricular hair cells between wild type and Stk32a +/- littermates.
claims.source: Furthermore, no differences were detected in the planar polarized organization of utricular hair cells between wild type and Stk32a +/- littermates (Figure 4—figure supplements 2–3).
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 4—figure supplements 2-3.

claims.claim: The planar polarized organization of vestibular hair cells in the medial regions of the Stk32a -/- utricle was severely disrupted.
claims.source: When evaluated by immunofluorescent labeling of βII-SPECTRIN at P5, it was evident that the planar polarized organization of vestibular hair cells in the medial regions of the Stk32a -/- utricle was severely disrupted (Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: Mutant hair cells in the striolar and medial extrastriolar regions of the Stk32a -/- utricle were randomly oriented relative to each other.
claims.source: Instead the bundles of hair cells in the striolar and medial extrastriolar regions of the Stk32a -/- utricle were randomly oriented relative to each other (Figure 4E–L)
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 4E-L.

claims.claim: Lateral hair cells in Stk32a -/- utricles remained correctly oriented.
claims.source: while lateral hair cells remained correctly oriented (Figure 4A–D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 4A-D.

claims.claim: Misoriented bundles were also seen in the outer region of the saccule and within the semi-circular canal cristae in Stk32a -/- mice.
claims.source: Misoriented bundles were also seen in the outer region of the saccule (Figure 4M–P) and within the semi-circular canal cristae (Figure 4Q-Bb); regions that normally express Stk32a and not Emx2.
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 4M-P and 4Q-Bb.

claims.claim: The extent of misorientation was greater in the maculae than in the cristae in Stk32a -/- mice.
claims.source: In general, the extent of misorientation was greater in the maculae than in the cristae though the basis for this difference is unknown.
claims.evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of bundle orientations shown in Figure 4.

claims.claim: Auditory hair cells were not impacted in Stk32a -/- cochleae.
claims.source: Auditory hair cells were not impacted in Stk32a -/- cochleae (Figure 4—figure supplement 4), most likely because they express Emx2 and not Stk32a (Jiang et al., 2017; Orvis et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4 and citations to prior literature.

claims.claim: The intrinsic polarity of the majority of vestibular hair cells remained intact in Stk32a -/- mice with kinocilium that were located on one side of the apical cell surface adjacent to the tallest row of stereocilia.
claims.source: Despite the randomization phenotype, the intrinsic polarity of the majority of vestibular hair cells remained intact with kinocilium that were located on one side of the apical cell surface adjacent to the tallest row of stereocilia (Figure 5A–B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 5A-B.

claims.claim: PK2 remains normally distributed in Stk32a -/- hair cells.
claims.source: For example PK2, which is asymmetrically distributed along one side of the hair cell (Deans et al., 2007), remains normally distributed in Stk32a -/- hair cells (Figure 5C–D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 5C-D and citation to prior literature.

claims.claim: In some Stk32a -/- hair cells, PK2 can be found on the side of the bundle rather than adjacent to or opposite of the kinocilium as seen in controls.
claims.source: As a result, in some Stk32a -/- hair cells, PK2 can be found on the side of the bundle rather than adjacent to or opposite of the kinocilium as seen in controls.
claims.evidence: This is based on observations of PK2 distribution in Stk32a -/- hair cells shown in Figure 5C-D.

claims.claim: The polarized distribution of CELSR1 at junctions between supporting cells is not altered in Stk32a -/-.
claims.source: In addition, the polarized distribution of CELSR1 at junctions between supporting cells is not altered in Stk32a -/- (Figure 5E, F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 5E, F.

claims.claim: Emx2 expression in the lateral extrastriolar region of the utricle and adjacent transitional epithelia was not impacted by Stk32a gene deletion.
claims.source: Emx2 expression in the lateral extrastriolar region of the utricle and adjacent transitional epithelia was also not impacted by Stk32a gene deletion (Figure 5G and H) consistent with this transcription factor acting upstream of Stk32a expression.
claims.evidence: This is supported by fluorescent in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 5G and H.

claims.claim: STK32A has a function in the medial utricle that coordinates intrinsic polarity of the hair cells with the PCP axis, and that is inhibited in the lateral utricle by EMX2.
claims.source: Together these observations demonstrate an STK32A function in the medial utricle that coordinates intrinsic polarity of the hair cells with the PCP axis, and that is inhibited in the lateral utricle by EMX2.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the integration of multiple experimental findings.

claims.claim: In the lateral region of the utricle and inner region of the saccule, EMX2 acts upstream of GPR156 to reorient stereociliary bundles and thereby position the LPR.
claims.source: In the lateral region of the utricle and inner region of the saccule, EMX2 acts upstream of the G-protein-coupled receptor GPR156 to reorient stereociliary bundles and thereby position the LPR (Kindt et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior literature.

claims.claim: GPR156 function is regulated post-translationally because it is expressed by all vestibular hair cells, but can only be detected at the apical hair cell surface in hair cells that also express Emx2.
claims.source: Remarkably, GPR156 function is regulated post-translationally because it is expressed by all vestibular hair cells, but can only be detected at the apical hair cell surface in hair cells that also express Emx2.
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge from prior work.

claims.claim: In controls, GPR156 was polarized apically in hair cells of the lateral utricle and inner saccule (Emx2-positive domains), but not in the rest of the organs (Emx2-negative domains).
claims.source: In controls, GPR156 was polarized apically in hair cells of the lateral utricle and inner saccule (Emx2-positive domains), but not in the rest of the organs (Emx2-negative domains), as reported previously (Figure 6A and C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 6A and C and reference to prior literature.

claims.claim: In Stk32a -/-, GPR156 was detected apically in the Emx2-negative domains of the utricle and saccule.
claims.source: In Stk32a -/-, however, GPR156 was also detected apically in the Emx2-negative domains of the utricle (Figure 6B) and saccule (Figure 6D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 6B and D.

claims.claim: GPR156 was detected at the cell boundary in Stk32a -/- cristae, but not in control cristae.
claims.source: Similarly, GPR156 was detected at the cell boundary in Stk32a -/- cristae, but not in control cristae as expected (Figure 6E and F and Kindt et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 6E and F and citation to prior literature.

claims.claim: Despite ectopic localization at apical cell boundaries in Emx2-negative hair cells, GPR156 was not tightly polarized as seen in control utricular cells on the lateral side of the LPR in Stk32a -/-.
claims.source: Despite ectopic localization at apical cell boundaries in Emx2-negative hair cells, GPR156 was not tightly polarized as seen in control utricular cells on the lateral side of the LPR, and was either symmetrical and surrounded individual cells, or was polarized but imprecisely aligned with the PCP axis (Figure 6B'', D'' and F'').
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunolabeling data shown in Figure 6B'', D'', F''.

claims.claim: Individual hair cells ectopically expressing Stk32a had decreased levels of GPR156 or displayed no GPR156 protein at their apical cell surface.
claims.source: Individual hair cells ectopically expressing Stk32a had decreased levels of GPR156 or displayed no GPR156 protein at their apical cell surface (Figure 7A, A', B and B').
claims.evidence: This is supported by electroporation and immunolabeling data shown in Figure 7A, A', B, B'.

claims.claim: A subset of Stk32a-P2A-EGFP expressing hair cells (8 of 50) had an inverted intrinsic planar polarity that was revealed by changes in the distribution of aPKC.
claims.source: In addition to changes in GPR156, a subset of Stk32a-P2A-EGFP expressing hair cells (8 of 50) also had an inverted intrinsic planar polarity that was revealed by changes in the distribution of aPKC (Figure 7C and C').
claims.evidence: This is supported by electroporation and immunolabeling data shown in Figure 7C, C'.

claims.claim: Auditory hair cells electroporated with constructs expressing the predicted kinase-dead Stk32a K52R mutant continued to display GPR156 protein at their apical cell boundaries.
claims.source: In contrast, auditory hair cells electroporated with constructs expressing the predicted kinase-dead Stk32a K52R mutant continued to display GPR156 protein at their apical cell boundaries (Figure 7D and D') suggesting that STK32A kinase activity is required for the negative regulation of GPR156 distribution.
claims.evidence: This is supported by electroporation and immunolabeling data shown in Figure 7D, D'.

claims.claim: The asymmetric distribution of GPR156 was impacted by the Stk32a K52R mutation because GPR156 could be detected at both the medial and lateral cell boundaries.
claims.source: Notably, the asymmetric distribution of GPR156 was also impacted by the Stk32a K52R mutation because GPR156 could be detected at both the medial and lateral cell boundaries (Figure 7D and F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by electroporation and immunolabeling data shown in Figure 7D, F.

claims.claim: STK32A is required for the post-translational regulation of GPR156 function through a phosphorylation-dependent event that regulates the presence of this receptor at the apical hair cell surface.
claims.source: Altogether, these gene deletion and electroporation-mediated overexpression assays demonstrate that STK32A is required for the post-translational regulation of GPR156 function through a phosphorylation-dependent event that regulates the presence of this receptor at the apical hair cell surface.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the integration of knockout and overexpression data.

claims.claim: GPR156 functions at the apical cell boundaries to align stereociliary bundles with the underlying PCP axis so that the basal body is positioned adjacent to PK2 in EMX2-positive regions of the utricle and saccule.
claims.source: In this model, GPR156 functions at the apical cell boundaries to align stereociliary bundles with the underlying PCP axis so that the basal body is positioned adjacent to PK2 in EMX2-positive regions of the utricle and saccule (Jiang et al., 2017; Kindt et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is part of a model proposed based on the integration of current and prior findings, supported by citations.

claims.claim: STK32A serves a similar function in EMX2-negative regions by positioning the basal body opposite of PK2.
claims.source: STK32A serves a similar function in EMX2-negative regions by positioning the basal body opposite of PK2 though the targets of STK32A kinase activity at this step remain unknown.
claims.evidence: This is part of a model proposed based on the experimental findings.

claims.claim: The LPR is formed along the boundary of Emx2 expression and is maintained by hair cells through two steps of negative regulation.
claims.source: The LPR is formed along the boundary of Emx2 expression and is maintained by hair cells through two steps of negative regulation.
claims.evidence: This is part of a model proposed based on the experimental findings.

claims.claim: STK32A inhibits GPR156 delivery or retention at the apical boundary of cells located on the medial, EMX2-negative side of the LPR.
claims.source: In the first, STK32A inhibits GPR156 delivery or retention at the apical boundary of cells located on the medial, EMX2-negative side of the LPR.
claims.evidence: This is part of a model proposed based on the experimental findings.

claims.claim: EMX2 represses Stk32a transcription in those hair cells located on the EMX2-positive side of the LPR, allowing GPR156 to accumulate at the cell surface where it can promote Emx2-dependent bundle reversal.
claims.source: In the second, EMX2 represses Stk32a transcription in those hair cells located on the EMX2-positive side of the LPR, allowing GPR156 to accumulate at the cell surface where it can promote Emx2-dependent bundle reversal.
claims.evidence: This is part of a model proposed based on the experimental findings.

claims.claim: Intercellular PCP signaling functions solely to align neighboring cells along a common polarity axis and is not impacted by Emx2, Gpr156 or Stk32a mutations.
claims.source: An essential tenet of this model is that intercellular PCP signaling functions solely to align neighboring cells along a common polarity axis and is not impacted by Emx2, Gpr156 or Stk32a mutations as has been shown previously (Jiang et al., 2017; Kindt et al., 2021 and Figure 5).
claims.evidence: This is part of the model and is supported by prior work and data in Figure 5.

claims.claim: The final position of the basal body and kinocilium relative to the core PCP proteins are determined by STK32A or GPR156.
claims.source: In this model, the final position of the basal body and kinocilium relative to the core PCP proteins are determined by STK32A or GPR156.
claims.evidence: This is part of the model proposed based on the experimental findings.

claims.claim: Prior transcriptional profiling has shown that EMX2 contributes to both transcriptional activation and repression in the developing telencephalon prior to cortical arealization.
claims.source: Prior transcriptional profiling has shown that EMX2 contributes to both transcriptional activation and repression in the developing telencephalon prior to cortical arealization (Hamasaki et al., 2004; Li et al., 2006)
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claims.claim: DNA binding assays have shown that EMX2 is capable of occupying POU sites in the Sox2 enhancer and repressing Sox2 expression in a dose-dependent manner.
claims.source: DNA binding assays have shown that EMX2 is capable of occupying POU sites in the Sox2 enhancer and repressing Sox2 expression in a dose-dependent manner (Mariani et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior literature.

claims.claim: EMX2 represses Gsx2 gene expression during earlier stages of telecephalic development but only in the presence of DMRT3 and DMRT5.
claims.source: The positive and negative regulation of gene expression may also be determined by cofactors since EMX2 represses Gsx2 gene expression during earlier stages of telecephalic development but only in the presence of DMRT3 and DMRT5 (Desmaris et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior literature.

claims.claim: The appearance of randomly oriented bundles in the medial region of the mutant utricle and outer region of the saccule suggests that one function of STK32A is to align bundle orientation with the PCP axis.
claims.source: The appearance of randomly oriented bundles in the medial region of the mutant utricle and outer region of the saccule suggests that one function is to align bundle orientation with the PCP axis.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the Stk32a knockout phenotype.

claims.claim: In Stk32a -/- hair cells the basal body either moves incorrectly relative to the PCP axis or is not maintained in a fixed position following an initially correct movement.
claims.source: Thus, in Stk32a -/- hair cells the basal body either moves incorrectly relative to the PCP axis or is not maintained in a fixed position following an initially correct movement.
claims.evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism underlying the Stk32a knockout phenotype.

claims.claim: The addition of STK32A dramatically reduces the amount of GPR156 detected at apical cell boundaries in cochlear hair cells.
claims.source: Although not normally expressed in these cells, the addition of STK32A dramatically reduces that amount of GPR156 detected at apical cell boundaries.
claims.evidence: This is supported by electroporation data shown in Figure 7.

claims.claim: STK32A could regulate GPR156 either by regulating a key step of GPR156 trafficking and delivery to the cell surface, or by activating the internalization of GPR156 from the cell surface after delivery has occurred.
claims.source: STK32A could do this either by regulating a key step of GPR156 trafficking and delivery to the cell surface, or by activating the internalization of GPR156 from the cell surface after delivery has occurred.
claims.evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism by which STK32A regulates GPR156.

claims.claim: The distribution of GPR156 in Stk32a -/- hair cells on the EMX2-negative side of the LPR does not have the same uniform planar polarized distribution that characterizes GPR156 distribution in hair cells that have EMX2.
claims.source: It should be noted however, that the distribution the GPR156 in Stk32a -/- hair cells on the EMX2-negative side of the LPR does not have the same uniform planar polarized distribution that characterizes GPR156 distribution in hair cells that have EMX2.
claims.evidence: This is based on observations of GPR156 distribution in Stk32a -/- shown in Figure 6.

claims.claim: The disorganized distribution of GPR156 in Stk32a -/- raises an alternative possibility that STK32A only has one function during hair cell development which is to negatively regulate GPR156.
claims.source: The disorganized distribution of GPR156 also raises an alternative possibility that STK32A only has one function during hair cell development which is to negatively regulate GPR156.
claims.evidence: This is speculation about an alternative model for STK32A function.

claims.claim: In an alternative scenario, the misoriented stereociliary bundles seen in Stk32a -/- would not be due to an STK32A function in regulating the position of the kinocilium but would be an artifact of GPR156 which does not normally function in these cells.
claims.source: In this scenario, the misoriented stereociliary bundles seen in Stk32a -/- would not be due to an STK32A function in regulating the position of the kinocilium. Instead the disorganization could be an artifact of GPR156 which does not normally function in these cells, is lacking a planar polarized organization, and could therefore disrupt the proper positioning of the kinocilium.
claims.evidence: This is speculation about an alternative explanation for the Stk32a knockout phenotype.

claims.claim: Predictions based on sequence analysis suggest that SKT32A is membrane-associated due to the potential for myristoylation of an N-terminal glycine.
claims.source: Predictions based on sequence analysis suggest that SKT32A is membrane-associated due to the potential for myristoylation of an N-terminal glycine (UniProt Consortium, 2021; UniProt C, 2023).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to sequence databases.

claims.claim: EGFP-tagged STK32A is present in stereocilia and at the apical cell surface and this localization is lost following deletion of the N-terminal glycine.
claims.source: Our observations that EGFP-tagged STK32A is present in stereocilia and at the apical cell surface and that this localization is lost following deletion of the N-terminal glycine, is consistent with myristoylation-dependent targeting to this location.
claims.evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3.

claims.claim: The apical localization of STK32A would be most consistent with an STK32A function to promote the internalization of GPR156 from the apical cell boundary rather than trafficking and delivery to that location.
claims.source: This apical localization of STK32A would be most consistent with an STK32A function to promote the internalization of GPR156 from the apical cell boundary rather than trafficking and delivery to that location.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the localization of STK32A.

claims.claim: STK32A has been predicted to localize to cilia.
claims.source: Alternatively, STK32A has been predicted to localize to cilia (Atlas THP, 2022; Thul et al., 2017)
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

results.result: STK32A is identified as a downstream effector negatively regulated by EMX2 in vestibular hair cells. RNAseq analysis of Emx2 mutant utricles revealed that Stk32a is upregulated in the absence of Emx2, and Stk32a expression is spatially complementary to Emx2 expression. Ectopic Emx2 expression reduces Stk32a levels, confirming transcriptional repression.
results.evaluation: Claims C5, C6, C36, C39, C40, C46-C49, and C118 collectively demonstrate that STK32A is negatively regulated by EMX2 through RNAseq data (C36, C39), spatial expression patterns (C6, C40, C46-C47), and gain-of-function experiments (C48). The complementary expression domains and expansion of Stk32a in Emx2 mutants provide strong converging evidence for transcriptional repression.

results.result: STK32A is necessary to align intrinsic hair cell polarity with the PCP axis in EMX2-negative regions. Stk32a knockout mice show randomly oriented hair cell bundles in medial utricle, outer saccule, and cristae, while lateral (EMX2-positive) hair cells remain correctly oriented. Intrinsic polarity and core PCP protein distribution remain intact in mutants.
results.evaluation: Claims C7, C34, C62-C75, and C97 provide strong evidence from loss-of-function studies. The knockout phenotype shows region-specific misorientation (C64-C68) in EMX2-negative domains while preserving intrinsic polarity (C70) and PCP protein distribution (C71-C73). The specificity of the phenotype to Stk32a-expressing regions and preservation of Emx2 expression (C74) support the necessity claim.

results.result: STK32A is sufficient to reorient hair cell bundles when ectopically expressed in EMX2-positive regions. AAV-mediated overexpression of Stk32a in lateral utricle hair cells causes bundle reorientation to resemble medial hair cells. This effect requires kinase activity (K52R mutant is inactive) and apical localization (Δ2G mutant lacking myristoylation is inactive).
results.evaluation: Claims C8, C50-C61 demonstrate sufficiency through gain-of-function experiments. AAV overexpression data (C50) shows bundle reorientation, with age-dependent effects (C51-C52) suggesting developmental timing requirements. Structure-function analysis with kinase-dead (C53-C54) and localization mutants (C58-C60) provides mechanistic insight. STK32A::EGFP localization to apical compartment and stereocilia (C55-C57) supports functional relevance.

results.result: STK32A regulates GPR156 localization at the apical hair cell surface. In Stk32a knockout mice, GPR156 appears ectopically at apical boundaries in EMX2-negative hair cells where it is normally absent. Ectopic STK32A expression in cochlear hair cells reduces GPR156 at apical boundaries in a kinase-dependent manner. This regulation establishes the position of the LPR.
results.evaluation: Claims C9, C35, C76-C86, C90-C91, C99, and C101 demonstrate STK32A regulation of GPR156 through complementary loss- and gain-of-function experiments. Knockout data (C79-C81) shows ectopic GPR156 in Stk32a-negative regions, while overexpression (C82, C84-C85, C99) shows GPR156 reduction requiring kinase activity. The disorganized GPR156 distribution in mutants (C81, C101) suggests additional regulatory factors may be involved, but the primary regulatory relationship is well-supported.

results.result: The authors propose a model where bundle orientation is determined through separate mechanisms on opposite sides of the LPR, with EMX2-mediated repression of Stk32a determining LPR position. In EMX2-positive regions, GPR156 positions the kinocilium adjacent to PK2; in EMX2-negative regions, STK32A positions it opposite to PK2. STK32A inhibits GPR156 localization in medial regions, while EMX2 represses Stk32a to allow GPR156 accumulation laterally.
results.evaluation: Claims C10, C87-C93, and C120-C122 present an integrated model supported by the experimental findings. The model is consistent with the complementary expression patterns (C5-C6), necessity (C7, C64-C67) and sufficiency (C8, C50) data for STK32A, and GPR156 regulation (C9, C79-C86). The model appropriately acknowledges that PCP signaling remains intact (C92) and that the final kinocilium position is determined by STK32A or GPR156 (C93). While some mechanistic details remain unknown (e.g., STK32A substrates in C88), the overall model is well-supported by the data.

results.result: Genes downregulated in Emx2 mutants (Slc26a4, Caln1, Stk26) are expressed in transitional epithelium rather than hair cells, suggesting EMX2 has broader roles beyond hair cell planar polarity.
results.evaluation: Claims C37-C38 and C119 are supported by RNAseq and in situ hybridization data showing these genes are in transitional epithelium, not hair cells. This observation correctly identifies that not all EMX2-regulated genes are relevant to hair cell polarity and supports the broader regulatory role proposed in C120-C121.

results.result: Stk32a is expressed in hair cells of the medial utricle and semi-circular canal cristae, regions where hair cells lack EMX2 and orient their kinocilia opposite to PK2.
results.evaluation: Claims C43-C45 are supported by fluorescent in situ hybridization data showing Stk32a colocalization with hair cell marker Gfi1 in these specific regions. The correlation with EMX2-negative, PK2-opposite orientation is supported by prior literature (C45) and consistent with the overall model.

results.result: Auditory hair cells in the cochlea are not affected in Stk32a knockout mice because they express Emx2 and not Stk32a.
results.evaluation: Claim C69 is supported by immunolabeling data and citations showing cochlear hair cells express Emx2 but not Stk32a. This provides an internal control demonstrating specificity of the Stk32a knockout phenotype to Stk32a-expressing regions.

results.result: STK32A is classified as a 'dark kinase' - a member of the STK32/YANK family with previously unknown biological function and substrates, related to AGC kinases by sequence homology.
results.evaluation: Claims C32, C41-C42, and C110-C112 accurately describe the classification of STK32A based on established literature. These are background claims supported by appropriate citations that contextualize the novelty of the findings.

results.result: Prior studies show EMX2 can function as both transcriptional activator and repressor in telencephalic development, with context-dependent mechanisms including cofactor requirements.
results.evaluation: Claims C94-C96 accurately summarize prior literature on EMX2 function in other developmental contexts. These citations provide precedent for EMX2 acting as a transcriptional repressor, supporting the interpretation of Stk32a regulation, though they do not directly demonstrate the mechanism in hair cells.

results.result: STK32A is predicted to be membrane-associated through N-terminal myristoylation. EGFP-tagged STK32A localizes to stereocilia and apical cell surface, and this localization is lost when the N-terminal glycine is deleted, consistent with myristoylation-dependent targeting.
results.evaluation: Claims C104-C106 are supported by sequence analysis predictions and experimental data showing localization of STK32A::EGFP and loss of localization in the Δ2G mutant. The inference about myristoylation-dependent targeting (C105) is reasonable given the sequence prediction and functional data, though direct biochemical confirmation of myristoylation is not provided.

results.result: STK32A has been predicted to localize to cilia and may associate with the chaperonin-containing T-complex (TRiC), which is involved in BBSome formation and ciliogenesis.
results.evaluation: Claims C107-C109 cite prior predictions and proteomic data but do not provide direct experimental validation in the current study. While these observations are consistent with a potential ciliary function for STK32A, they remain speculative without additional experimental support. The authors appropriately present these as alternative possibilities rather than established facts.

results.result: Alternative mechanistic interpretations are discussed, including whether STK32A has dual functions (aligning bundles with PCP axis and regulating GPR156) or a single function (regulating GPR156, with misorientation being a secondary consequence).
results.evaluation: Claims C98, C100, C102-C103 present speculative alternative models that the authors acknowledge cannot be definitively distinguished with current data. These represent honest scientific uncertainty about mechanism rather than supported conclusions. The disorganized GPR156 distribution in Stk32a mutants (C101) suggests the mechanism may be more complex than either simple model.

results.result: STK32A has been linked to cancer (stomach adenocarcinoma, neuroendocrine carcinoma, metastatic melanoma) in prior studies, and disrupted planar cell polarity is associated with cancer progression. Small molecule inhibitors of STK32A have been identified.
results.evaluation: Claims C113-C114, C116-C117 accurately cite prior literature connecting STK32A to cancer and noting the availability of small molecule tools. These are contextual claims that suggest potential translational relevance but are not experimentally validated in the current study.

results.result: Background claims about vestibular hair cell structure, function, and planar polarity organization, including the roles of intrinsic polarity, PCP signaling, and EMX2/GPR156 in establishing the LPR.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C3, C11-C31 represent established background knowledge supported by appropriate citations to prior literature. These provide necessary context for understanding the current study but are not novel findings. The claims accurately represent the state of knowledge in the field.
